WE ARE STILL ON THE JOURNEY TO PHASING OUT BSI PROGRAMS AND CONTINUOUSLY WORKING TO SUPPORT EDUCATORS ACROSS EVERY SCHOOL COMMUNITY TO IMPLEMENT DSC APPROVED PROGRAMING.
AND IT IS ONE OF THE MODELS THAT THE STATE HAS APPROVED FOR EDUCATING STUDENTS WHO ARE LEARNING ENGLISH AS A SECOND LANGUAGE.
AND COUNCILOR FLYNN, YOUR CONCERNS ARE REAL.

BUT WHAT I CAN SAY IS IN OUR DUAL LANGUAGE BILINGUAL EDUCATION CLASSROOM THAT HAS BEEN APPROVED BY DC OUT OF THE OFFICE OF LANGUAGE ACQUISITION, WE AIM FOR A 5050 UH 50% ENGLISH DOMINANT STUDENTS AND UH 50% PARTNER LANGU
AND SO IF WE COULD ALSO THINK ABOUT SORT OF HOW TO MAKE THESE DUAL LAYERED PROGRAMS MORE ACCESSIBLE TO THOSE WHO LIVE ACROSS THE CITY, I THINK THAT IS A MAJOR CONCERN.
MEAN THIS QUESTION WAS ASKED A FEW MINUTES AGO ABOUT BSI UM DELINEATING BETWEEN BSI AND THEN THE STATE APPROVED CI.

IN ADDITION, IS RECENTLY APPROVED OPPORTUNITY AND ACHIEVEMENT GAPS POLICY STATES QUOTE BPA SHALL AFFIRM THE CULTURAL AND LINGUISTIC ASSETS OF MULTILINGUAL LEARNERS AND MOVE WITH ALL DELIBERATE SPEED TO STRENGTHEN BILINGU

A MAJORITY OF BOSTON VOTERS AND THEIR LEADERS INCLUDING THE MAYOR, THE CHAIR OF THE SCHOOL COMMITTEE AND THE SUPERINTENDENT ALL OPPOSED THAT REFERENDUM.

FOURTH, WITH THE LOOK ACT PASSED IN 2017, WE GAIN MORE FLEXIBILITY TO USE HOME LANGUAGE AND INSTRUCTION AND WITH THE RECENT EDUCATOR DIVERSITY ACT WE GAIN MORE FLEXIBILITY TO BRING BILINGUAL EDUCATORS BACK AFTER MORE THA
MANY MOTHERS ARE VERY CONCERNED WITH THE PROBLEM WITH THE IEPS.

SINCE THAT CHANGE, WE HEAR FROM EDUCATORS ABOUT THEIR CONCERN FOR THE STUDENTS IN THEIR CLASS WHO ARE MULTILINGUAL LEARNERS AND THEY SHARE CONCERNS ABOUT HOW TO MODIFY INSTRUCTION APPROPRIATELY FOR THE VARIETY OF LANGUAG
AS A MOTHER I'M CONCERNED BECAUSE I SEE THAT I'M NOT THE ONLY ONE IN MEETINGS A LOT OF PEOPLE ARE EXPRESSING THE SAME CONCERNS.
